research_title: Android/mobile navigation and search in a large personal time-tracking catalogue
scope: Mobile catalogue discovery, search, synonym/typo/multilingual retrieval, favorites/recents, folder/tree and facet navigation, user-setting transfer, and Android accessibility. This is research, not an implementation or product-scope approval.
constraints_observed: Read the four requested prior research documents before researching; see read_before.
Did not install apps or alter code, pages, app settings, or accounts.
Did not spawn or delegate to other agents.
Distinguish observed user report, vendor/product claim, research inference, and untested hypothesis.
Do not convert privacy/security into a restriction on the user's right to record arbitrary personal activities locally.
Continuation: refreshed official Clockify help/changelog and read the supplied core/UI/catalog contracts. No app/device/user test, code, UI, settings change or new agent was involved.

read_before.existing_coverage: Starter set and one-tap start, optional details, favorites/recent, progressive disclosure, several competitor patterns.
read_before.incremental_scope: Mobile search-entry point, long-list and recent-order pain, typeahead performance, personal setting export boundary, Unicode and TalkBack details.

read_before.existing_coverage: Tree versus tags, mobile large-list gap, safe history reorganization.
read_before.incremental_scope: Search in current versus global scope, paths in result rows, empirical user reports on mobile search, tag filter patterns, accessible reorder.

read_before.read: full file; relevant selection/search and model sections additionally inspected
read_before.existing_coverage: Quick actions, search, favorites/recents, locally bundled synonyms, no auto-classification, data model and preliminary accessibility.
read_before.incremental_scope: Evidence for mobile catalogue navigation; ranking and localization safeguards; access/migration and performance scenarios.

read_before.existing_coverage: Stable identity, aliases, local-first and data-safety issues.
read_before.incremental_scope: Catalogue-only settings portability distinct from time history, with Android community/product examples.

read_before.existing_coverage: Static summary of supported ActivityType, aliases, history path, axes/metrics/units and addCatalog conflicts.
read_before.incremental_scope: Separate documented support from proposed recent/pins/catalog-only portable contract.

read_before.existing_coverage: Current UI/core operations, saveFavorite/startFavorite, history, backup and restore behavior.
read_before.incremental_scope: Exact boundary between current selection-snapshot favorites and proposed item favorites, Recent, detail pins and start presets.

read_before.existing_coverage: One-tree catalog semantics, IDs/history, merge statuses, backup/restore boundary.
read_before.incremental_scope: Stable-ID import contract, user override conflict precedence, no-history-rewrite conditions.

claim_taxonomy.meaning: First-person experience, pain, or request in a thread or review; evidence of a use case, not prevalence.
Official support page, release note, or vendor statement documents product behavior or intent; it is not an independent usability result.
Official Android/Unicode guidance informs testable implementation requirements.
Design conclusion reasoned from multiple evidence items and prior project decisions.
Plausible design behavior needing user/device evaluation; not established fact.
Behavior stated in the supplied core/UI/product contract or static compatibility review; documented behavior, not hands-on device verification.
A deterministic, reversible design recommendation authored in this follow-up; not implemented or approved.

sources.title: TimeTac Android App Guide, PDF
sources.date_or_version: PDF crawled 2026; document is older (search metadata ~5.8 years)
sources.read_scope: Opened 22-page/475-line PDF and read the mobile section including Projects & Tasks, hierarchy, search, Recent/Favourites/All, and adjacent app structure. No hands-on app test.
sources.finding: The phone picker has search suggestions, tabs To-Dos/Favourites/Recent/All, breadcrumb/superior-level row, folder browsing, and inline start/stop for tasks.
sources.limitation: Enterprise app; documentation age and current native screen version were not hands-on verified. Vendor documentation, not independent usability evidence.

sources.title: aTimeLogger Activities
sources.read_scope: Read relevant full help page covering start/stop, hidden groups, full display path, and multiple activities.
sources.finding: Groups may be hidden from the frequent Activities screen while types remain visible; a display-path setting disambiguates duplicate child names.
sources.limitation: The docs note most screenshots/menu paths refer to iOS even where behavior also exists on Android; this page is not a hands-on Android verification.

sources.title: aTimeLogger Types and Groups
sources.read_scope: Read the full page, including group display/order, archive and destructive conversion/deletion lifecycle.
sources.finding: Users can hide groups, order manually or by name, reorder nested items, and inspect their statistics; product distinguishes logged types from grouping nodes.
sources.limitation: Evidence of described feature set only; deleting/conversion implications already overlap the prior hierarchy/reliability work.

sources.title: aTimeLogger History
sources.read_scope: Read complete substantive sections for history navigation, filters, search and export.
sources.finding: History search covers activity type name, comment, or tags inside the selected date range; type/tag filters are separate.
sources.limitation: This is search across recorded history, not proof of search in the start catalogue.

sources.title: aTimeLogger FAQ
sources.read_scope: Read full FAQ portions on sync, offline use, data export, account and platform sharing.
sources.finding: Vendor says it syncs changes across supported devices with Premium Sync and remains usable offline; it separately distinguishes local-only usage from account-backed sync.
sources.limitation: Vendor claim, not verified migration or backup test; no field-by-field setting payload was documented.

sources.title: ATracker task creation and task/task-entry distinction
sources.read_scope: Read complete substantive help text.
sources.finding: Reusable tasks and time-entry records are explicitly separate; tasks can be created from Today/Admin.
sources.limitation: Does not document a global activity catalogue search.

sources.title: ATracker compact Today task list
sources.read_scope: Located and read the compact-view support entry; full app behavior not hands-on tested.
sources.finding: Compact task presentation is an explicit option on the Today screen.
sources.limitation: The page describes feature setup, not a measured optimum grid density or accessibility performance.

sources.title: ATracker reorder tasks
sources.read_scope: Read complete procedure.
sources.finding: Today tasks support drag-and-drop reordering and alphabetical order.
sources.limitation: Does not establish accessibility of drag-and-drop or usability with hundreds of items.

sources.title: ATracker Feature request - frequently used icons
sources.date_or_version: Started 2021; new exchange in 2025; latest visible maintainer response Aug 3, 2025
sources.read_scope: Search result rendered the complete seven-comment thread. Direct open returned Cache miss, so do not count it as direct full-page access.
sources.finding: Users report repeatedly scrolling to find reused tasks in a long list and painful manual relocation; the team discussed recent/frequency sorting but noted time-window ambiguity, offered tag filter/manual sort, and said request remained to-do in 2025.
sources.limitation: Single/limited users and old feature status; does not measure prevalence, and 2026 live app was not installed/retested.

sources.title: ATracker tag filtering and help index
sources.read_scope: Read listed help topics for Today, task/tag filter, search history, compact view, and ordering.
sources.finding: Documentation separates Today tag filtering from History search of task entries.
sources.limitation: An index documents page availability, not all screen details; tag filtering is not tree navigation.

sources.title: ATracker Android backup/restore
sources.read_scope: Read full substantive steps for Android-to-Android backup/restore.
sources.finding: Android transfer is file based and may require a PC because some vendors restrict direct file access.
sources.limitation: Does not state field-by-field whether favorite order, aliases, and all UI preferences are included.

sources.title: ATracker migration iOS and Android
sources.read_scope: Read complete substantive page.
sources.finding: Vendor says direct cross-platform database transfer is unsupported; web sync can convert structure, with subscription requirement stated.
sources.limitation: Historic vendor policy and data migration, not only catalogue settings.

sources.title: ATracker Sharing task list discussion
sources.read_scope: Complete two-post thread returned in search result.
sources.finding: User requests sharing the task list independently. Maintainer describes database export as including all tasks and task entries and says that is not feasible with many time entries; Android/iOS formats differ.
sources.limitation: Short historical discussion. A participant's mention of sensitive data is not a policy or a reason to restrict arbitrary private logging.

sources.title: Clockify Find projects/tasks quickly
sources.date_or_version: Official page opened 2026-10-11; crawler reported 4 days earlier
sources.read_scope: Re-opened and read full substantive sections (lines 22-54) on 2026-10-11: compact project list, project/task favorites, and task filter.
sources.finding: Current help: compact project list for hundreds of clients/projects/tasks; project favorites at the top of finder are user-specific but require workspace activation; Task filter is user-specific web-profile setting and supports task@project/client scope.
sources.limitation: Official documentation of web preference/finder behavior; not an Android hands-on test and not proof of usability.

sources.title: Clockify profile preferences for project collapse and task filter
sources.date_or_version: Official page opened 2026-10-11; crawler reported 2 days earlier
sources.read_scope: Re-opened and read full applicable preference and FAQ text (lines 75-103, 169-171) on 2026-10-11.
sources.finding: Collapse preference offers collapse all / none / collapse above project count; task filter is enabled in Profile settings > Preferences; FAQ explains task name in description field followed by @project.
sources.limitation: The page describes web profile settings; it does not document the exact Android picker interaction.

sources.title: Clockify Android feature request: search in Time entries window
sources.read_scope: Search result rendered all four posts (original user, vendor questions, explanation, vendor reply).
sources.finding: Interrupt-driven user says returning to a past task requires several navigation steps; asks to search prior tasks from the Android time-entry window and preselect the last-used task; vendor says autocomplete is being developed.
sources.limitation: Historical request and promise, not current Android app status or outcome.

sources.title: Clockify Universal Search for Project OR Task
sources.read_scope: Search result rendered all ten visible posts (the forum count is original + nine replies), including mobile-specific and ~100-project/~40-task reports.
sources.finding: Users report empty results when search assumes the wrong object type, unintuitive @ syntax and long mobile lists; a scaling example had nearly 100 projects with up to 40 tasks each.
sources.limitation: Historic enterprise use cases and status; not prevalence or current product state.

sources.title: Clockify Favorite and/or Recent Descriptions
sources.read_scope: Opened and read all lines; two total posts.
sources.finding: User wants to type/select recently used description scoped to currently selected project; vendor says suggestion passed to product team.
sources.limitation: No implementation status in thread.

sources.title: Toggl Track Favorites product announcement
sources.read_scope: Read product feature description and platform availability statement.
sources.finding: A favorite can start an entire pre-populated time entry on Android, not just a named category.
sources.limitation: Paid-plan feature with platform-gate history; product claim, not measured UX.

sources.title: Simple Time Tracker releases
sources.read_scope: Read current release listing; examined v1.52-v1.59 and recent search/tag/category entries.
sources.finding: Main-tab search, tag selection search, categories/tags relations view and per-activity favorite comments arrived incrementally in separate releases.
sources.limitation: Changelog documents shipped capabilities, not discoverability or satisfaction; unrelated release items excluded.

sources.title: Simple Time Tracker issue: lag with Similar comments open
sources.read_scope: Opened the full issue description; search result also displayed maintainer and user follow-up. Full issue activity log could not be retrieved from the page view.
sources.finding: One user reports lag and lost second/third typed characters with a very large result set; an almost 10,000-comment crafted backup reproduces a typeahead performance issue in activity-start comment input. The user says v1.59/local dev remained slow in that field after an attempted improvement.
sources.limitation: Issue concerns similar comments, not the activity catalogue; reproducer is user supplied and not run by this research. Full comment-log access not confirmed.

sources.title: Simple Time Tracker: Are template activities translatable?
sources.read_scope: Opened the complete discussion: original question, answer, and acknowledgment.
sources.finding: Seeded template labels (e.g., lunch, dinner, work, sleep) were English-only at time of answer; maintainer planned translation.
sources.limitation: Not about user-generated label translation/search. Historical state only.

sources.title: Simple Time Tracker: Why are strings forced to lower case?
sources.read_scope: Opened all eight thread comments.
sources.finding: French volunteer translator questions forced lower-case presentation in a goal hint/notification; maintainer explains design intent for a non-sentence label. This demonstrates locale presentation context, not a catalogue-name search defect.
sources.limitation: Only adjacent localization evidence; deliberately not generalized to custom activity names.

sources.title: Simple Time Tracker: Tool to migrate from Timelog
sources.read_scope: Opened complete two-post thread.
sources.finding: User built a JSON-to-CSV migration tool, describing conversion as local in-browser; maintainer appreciates it.
sources.limitation: Tool was not run; one user's solution, history migration rather than settings-only transfer.

sources.title: Android per-app language preferences
sources.read_scope: Read descriptions of app-language settings on Android 13+, APIs and migration/back-up notes.
sources.finding: Android permits a user-selected per-app UI language and supports system/API synchronization; it does not translate application content automatically.
sources.limitation: Platform/UI language help does not solve user-label search or synonym handling.

sources.title: Unicode Collation Algorithm (UTS #10)
sources.date_or_version: Version 14.0 / revision 45 (2021); current stable report linked from Unicode
sources.read_scope: Read specification summary and sections on linguistic/language variation in collation and loose searching.
sources.finding: Sort/search equivalences vary by locale; a single universal accent/character policy is not linguistically correct for every language.
sources.limitation: Normative/reference technical guidance, not a user study.

sources.title: Unicode Normalization Forms (UTR #15)
sources.date_or_version: Current revision accessible via latest report link
sources.read_scope: Read normalization/equivalence overview and caution on compatibility normalization.
sources.finding: Normalization helps compare equivalent encodings, but compatibility transformations may erase visually meaningful distinctions and should not blindly replace arbitrary display text.
sources.limitation: Technical guidance, not a product-specific acceptance benchmark.

sources.title: Unicode LDML Collation
sources.read_scope: Read relevant matching strengths/ignore accents and punctuation notes.
sources.finding: Case, accent and punctuation matching can be configured as separate strengths.
sources.limitation: Does not prescribe one right product setting for this user.

sources.title: 2Do Android search help
sources.read_scope: Read full search overview, matching modes, search scope and saved-search description.
sources.finding: Vendor offers exact/full-text search separately from Soundex matching, explains typo examples, and allows scope/presets.
sources.limitation: Adjacent to time tracking, not evidence that Soundex generalizes to Russian/multilingual catalogues.

sources.title: Jetpack Compose accessibility API defaults
sources.read_scope: Read minimum touch target, graphic description, and semantic merge sections.
sources.finding: Interactive elements should meet minimum 48dp target; labels and semantics need to reach accessibility services.
sources.limitation: API guidance, not an audit of the tracker UI.

sources.title: Android Text scaling accessibility help
sources.read_scope: Read design and test guidance for text scaling and responsive layouts.
sources.finding: Use scalable text and avoid fixed constraints that crop/obscure large font; test maximum font in portrait/landscape.
sources.limitation: General platform guidance, no actual catalogue screenshot test.

sources.title: TalkBack navigation and container navigation for long lists/grids
sources.read_scope: Read section for container navigation and list/grid movement.
sources.finding: TalkBack has navigation to escape long list/grid containers; the catalogue must be tested with a screen reader in addition to touch.
sources.limitation: System capability, not proof of an app-level deficiency.

sources.title: Compose custom accessibility actions
sources.read_scope: Read custom-action guidance and examples for gestures/list items.
sources.finding: Complex gestures such as drag-and-drop/swipe may be difficult for some users; equivalent named custom actions can be exposed through accessibility services.
sources.limitation: Guidance does not determine which reorder controls are best for this product.

sources.title: Compose SearchBar
sources.read_scope: Read search query state, suggestions and result-selection examples.
sources.finding: Provides a standard structure for an input field, suggestions and result list driven by query changes.
sources.limitation: UI component example; doesn't supply search ranking, language normalization, performance guarantee or typeahead interaction tests.

sources.title: Clockify Android app help
sources.date_or_version: Crawled 2026-10-11; official page says 30 min read
sources.read_scope: Opened full text (1,108 lines) and read relevant sections: time tracking and edit entry (lines 87-169), Android Track again widget (271-311), manage projects (742-790), profile/settings/default project/offline selection (791-900). No installation or device test.
sources.finding: Android help documents project/task as entry details, exact-detail continuation of previous entries, a Track again widget listing four most-recent entries, default fixed/last-used project, and selection of only previously loaded catalogue items offline. It does not document the detailed Android task-search/filter flow.
sources.limitation: Vendor documentation, not observed current UI; surrounding features may be workspace/permission dependent.

sources.title: Clockify official changelog
sources.date_or_version: Current page opened 2026-10-11; relevant entries Aug/Oct 2026
sources.read_scope: Opened current changelog full page and read current October, September, August, June and historical entries matching task/project picker and search (lines 18-119; 158-170).
sources.finding: October 2026 lists a fix for inability to remove a favorite entry on Time tracker. August 2026 lists Android search functionality issues when Task filter is active as a fix; June lists long project-name display issue in expanded picker.
sources.limitation: Release notes identify product issue/fix labels, but do not show exact UI, release build, regression tests or independently verified outcome; absence in a later month is not proof.

sources.title: Каталог и ядро v3: проверка совместимости (project artifact)
sources.date_or_version: 2026-10-11; static review of commit stated in the document
sources.read_scope: Read full document, including supported models, addCatalog result semantics, type IDs/aliases, history and remaining integration boundary.
sources.finding: Documents ActivityType stable ID/aliases/hierarchy, historical path, supported dictionaries and per-key ADDED/UNCHANGED/CONFLICT import outcome; distinguishes existing core capability from desired catalog/adapter work.
sources.limitation: Static compatibility document, not an independent run or live product UX.

sources.title: UI integration contract v2 (project artifact)
sources.read_scope: Read complete contract, especially saveFavorite/startFavorite/repeat, classification/history, JSON backup/restore, addCatalog and constraints.
sources.finding: Current contract states saveFavorite/startFavorite/removeFavorite saved selection snapshots; Repeat/Favorite preserve selected type/details and archived choices; whole-dataset JSON restore is replacement. No standalone recency, detail-pin or catalog-only transfer semantics are specified.
sources.limitation: Contract text does not prove UI/API implementation or user acceptance beyond what the document explicitly says.

sources.title: Единое дерево и словари · реализованный контракт v2 (project artifact)
sources.read_scope: Read entire file including tree, aliases, saved historical IDs/path, JSON backup/restore and import-conflict notes.
sources.finding: States addCatalog preserves existing local names/links on conflicts and may apply independent definitions; current full backup restore is explicit replacement; type meaning change requires a new ID; no name-based remap is provided.
sources.limitation: Implementation boundary document, not tested import or cross-device transfer.

evidence.statement: An Android time-tracker can combine a global activity/task search, recently/frequently accessible categories, hierarchy breadcrumbs, and inline start/stop in one picker.
evidence.strength: Direct vendor documentation of one product pattern.
evidence.caveat: TimeTac is enterprise-oriented and guide age is non-trivial; do not infer measured usability.

evidence.statement: A mobile search restricted to the wrong object type can produce no results; requiring a project choice then a task search and long scrolling can frustrate users, particularly in large lists.
evidence.strength: Two specific first-person vendor-community reports; one explicitly describes Android and another says the effect is particularly frustrating on mobile.
evidence.caveat: 2020 forum threads; historic behavior and a few workflows, not prevalence/current app status.

evidence.statement: Manual ordering is not a scalable substitute for fast access as tasks accumulate; users request recently or frequently used tasks and a way to move a selected item straight to the top.
evidence.strength: A user raised the request in 2021 and another added a detailed long-list case in 2025; maintainer discusses implementation trade-offs.
evidence.caveat: Narrow feature-request thread; not a broad usability study.

evidence.statement: Time entries, reusable task definitions, tree/group nodes, filter tags and history search have distinct product roles.
evidence.strength: Supported by several official help pages.
evidence.caveat: Documentation pages sometimes describe shared iOS/Android behavior but screenshots/menu paths are iOS-based.

evidence.statement: A user with frequent interruptions wants to find a previous task from the active Android timer/entry window; last-used default would save project-switching steps.
evidence.strength: Specific user-described task-switching journey in a full four-post thread.
evidence.caveat: One user's use case, historical product discussion.

evidence.statement: Search syntax that depends on whether the user means task, project, or client can fail to match the user's mental model; a person reported roughly 100 projects and up to 40 tasks each, with extra frustration on mobile.
evidence.strength: Full ten-post thread showed both original request and subsequent user examples.
evidence.caveat: Enterprise examples should not be assumed to match a personal tracker’s typical scale.

evidence.statement: A user values selecting a recent description scoped to an already selected project rather than retyping it.
evidence.strength: Full two-post discussion.
evidence.caveat: It concerns a time-entry description, not a task-definition favorite.

evidence.statement: The label Favorite can mean a stable project favorite or a one-tap fully prepopulated time entry; it is not inherently a synonym for recent activity.
evidence.strength: Three official product documentation/announcement sources document differing semantics.
evidence.caveat: Patterns differ by product tier and enterprise settings.

evidence.statement: Searching through activity types, searching history entries, and filtering by tags are separate affordances in mobile tracking products.
evidence.strength: Multiple official docs clearly describe scope separation.
evidence.caveat: Never infer that history search also covers every start-picker item.

evidence.statement: Autocomplete or similar comments can become too slow to type into when a high-cardinality suggestion set is rendered/queried; one user reported keystrokes being dropped with about 9,998 comments.
evidence.strength: Issue contains a detailed reproduction description and later user follow-up; release history separately shows search features added incrementally.
evidence.caveat: This is a comment-suggestion UI, not catalogue search; reproduction not run and issue activity log was only partially retrieved.

evidence.statement: Seed labels which don't localize with the surrounding interface may leave a multilingual user unable to understand first-run presets.
evidence.strength: Full user/maintainer discussion identifies English-only default templates as of Jan 2026.
evidence.caveat: Does not establish a problem for custom labels or search.

evidence.statement: UI language, user's label, alias, and search normalization are separate concerns; locale-sensitive comparisons should not silently rewrite displayed personal data.
evidence.strength: Derived from platform locale behavior and Unicode guidance.
evidence.caveat: The actual supported languages and match behavior need localization tests.

evidence.statement: Adjacent Android task software separates exact full-text search from phonetic typo-tolerant matching and saved search presets.
evidence.strength: Official product documentation with examples.
evidence.caveat: 2Do is not a time tracker; English Soundex behavior must not be assumed suitable for non-English labels.

evidence.statement: Some Android transfer routes copy a full database/history or require a web conversion subscription; one user's request for a task-list-only share was answered with a full-database export.
evidence.strength: Official migration help and complete community exchange; contrasting sync claim also documented.
evidence.caveat: Source states do not reveal whether all personal UI settings/order/aliases are included.

evidence.statement: Android activity grids/search results need tested focus semantics, explicit labels, 48dp touch targets, responsive text, and accessible alternatives to drag-only ordering.
evidence.strength: Multiple current official Android guidance pages.
evidence.caveat: No app-specific TalkBack user report was retrieved; these are test requirements, not observed defects.

evidence.statement: Combine a short stable quick-start layer, all-catalog search with full-path result labels, optional tree browse, and separate facet filters; do not require taxonomy setup to log.
evidence.strength: Converges documented patterns and user reports with the pre-existing progressive-UI/product-model proposal.
evidence.caveat: Promising synthesis, not validated in an interaction test.

evidence.statement: Exact name/alias, prefix, normalized case/accent, and finally a clearly marked fuzzy fallback will help multilingual typo searches without unacceptable false matches.
evidence.strength: Plausible implementation hypothesis informed by platform/adjacent product docs.
evidence.caveat: Needs language-specific test corpus and a decision about short query thresholds.

evidence.statement: Use explicit manual Favorite, timestamp-based Recent, and optional frequency ranking as separate concepts.
evidence.strength: Reasoned from official patterns and direct team explanation of frequency-window ambiguity.
evidence.caveat: Requires user test to decide which of these belongs in the default start screen.

evidence.statement: If catalog portability is added, make selected personal navigation/search settings exportable separately from recorded history; user selects payload explicitly.
evidence.strength: Reasoned from observed migration coupling and existing offline/data-export project direction.
evidence.caveat: Not a data-security restriction; exact bundle fields, conflicts, and current backups need product decision and testing.

evidence.statement: As of the official help pages opened 2026-10-11, Clockify describes compact project grouping for large catalogs, user-specific project favorites (enabled by workspace), and user-specific task filtering via web profile preferences using task@project/client syntax.
evidence.strength: Direct current vendor documentation read in full on this pass.
evidence.caveat: Does not show Android hands-on picker; feature presence is not a usability result.

evidence.statement: Clockify Android help documents exact-detail continuation of an old entry and a Track again widget that shows four most recently tracked entries; the Android project/task search UI itself is not specified in the relevant help sections.
evidence.strength: Direct official Android guide text.
evidence.caveat: Documentation may lag the live app; no app installed or exercised.

evidence.statement: Clockify official changelog lists an August 2026 fix item for Android search issues when Task filter is active, June 2026 long-name project-picker display issue, and an October 2026 fix item for removing a favorite entry on Time tracker.
evidence.strength: Current first-party release notes.
evidence.caveat: Release-note labels do not establish exact current behavior, build coverage, or independent fix verification.

evidence.statement: The supplied UI contract documents saveFavorite/startFavorite/removeFavorite and Repeat as saved selection/parameter snapshots; Repeat/Favorite keep selected type/details even after card rename/archive, and a new entry resolves its path at current tree at start.
evidence.strength: Directly stated in current project contract.
evidence.caveat: The exact stored Favorite field list and actual live UI have not been verified.

evidence.statement: Current core compatibility documents stable type IDs and aliases, saved ancestorPathAtWrite, dictionary axes/metrics/units, addCatalog per-key ADDED/UNCHANGED/CONFLICT outcomes and preservation of local conflicts. JSON v2 restore remains a full dataset replacement, not catalog-only merge.
evidence.strength: Direct static contract/document analysis.
evidence.caveat: No catalog-only payload/import adapter or real-device transfer has been run.

evidence.statement: Keep four distinct personal access objects: live item Favorite reference; Recent derived only from actual successful segment starts; context-scoped pinned detail value/text; named whole-entry start preset snapshot. Removing any access metadata must not remove the target item or logged history.
evidence.strength: Deterministic reversible recommendation informed by current core boundaries and documented competitor distinctions.
evidence.caveat: Not approved, implemented, or usability-tested; proposed eight-row Recent summary needs testing.

evidence.statement: A separately versioned catalog-only bundle should merge definitions and explicitly selected personal catalog settings by stable IDs, preserve destination overrides by default, report ID/meaning conflicts, and never include or rewrite time-history records. Full JSON restore is not suitable for this merge.
evidence.strength: Deterministic recommendation aligned to existing ID/history/restore contracts.
evidence.caveat: Schema, preview statuses and import adapter are new proposals, not current functionality.

needs.need: Find a known activity from the screen where the person starts or resumes tracking, without deciding in advance whether it is a project, task, group, or tag.
needs.design_response: Search all personal activity labels first; put query near Start/Now and let optional filters narrow later.

needs.need: Return quickly to a deliberately important activity and to a recently used activity.
needs.design_response: Stable manual Favorites and chronological Recent; keep frequency ranking optional.
needs.status: two different access signals established; exact layout/default not decided

needs.need: Re-find an item in hundreds or more records without scroll-only interaction or an obscure search syntax.
needs.design_response: Global query, indexed/local list, lazy result rendering and predictable ranking; load deeper matches on demand.
needs.status: an analogous large enterprise scale and a very large comment case exist; personal-catalog performance to measure

needs.need: Recognize the intended item when siblings/groups share a display name.
needs.design_response: Show path/breadcrumb in search rows and accessible labels; optionally hide group nodes from quick-start grid.
needs.status: product patterns documented; target hierarchy behavior to test

needs.need: Filter by an overlapping property without pretending the property is a folder or replacing the user's own name.
needs.design_response: Keep tree and tags/facets distinct; user-created activity remains loggable if unmatched.
needs.status: concept already aligned with prior model; mobile filter details remain to prototype

needs.need: Search labels even when the UI locale, script, accent, or user's shorthand differs.
needs.design_response: Separate UI translations, original personal label, and personal/local alias list; stage match strength without rewriting.
needs.status: requirements technically supported; target user languages and exact match policy are open

needs.need: Typeahead/autocomplete must not become slow or swallow characters at high result counts.
needs.design_response: Avoid eagerly creating thousands of tappable suggestion buttons; incremental/lazy rendering, measurable responsiveness, scope narrowing.
needs.status: analogous issue observed; size/latency envelope not benchmarked

needs.need: Move a favorite or change its order without relying exclusively on a drag gesture or visual icon/color.
needs.design_response: Expose explicitly named accessible row actions for pin/move-top/order and semantic Favorite state.
needs.status: platform guidance supports alternate actions; no tracker-specific motor/accessibility interview found

needs.need: Move one's own useful catalogue/navigation settings between devices without being forced to move all old history.
needs.design_response: Offer explicit settings/catalogue payload distinct from history; preserve local/offline tracking and allow the user to decide what to transfer.
needs.status: design inference; user need directly appears in a task-list sharing request, but item-specific transfer not field-tested

needs.need: Read/navigate and act on a long catalogue under TalkBack, Switch Access/Voice Access and enlarged text.
needs.design_response: Semantic full path/state, screen-reader traversal/escape, responsive text, large touch targets, and alternate reorder action.
needs.status: acceptance requirement, not observed user-report evidence

needs.need: Start an existing favorite quickly while preserving the intended surrounding fields where the user chose to save a full start.
needs.design_response: Keep activity favorite distinct from a whole-entry preset/favorite and show prefilled context before starting.
needs.status: vendor examples document the pattern; target need unvalidated

needs.need: Tell apart a favorite activity, a recently started activity, a pinned detail value, and a reusable full selection/start preset.
needs.design_response: Expose separate nouns and independent lifecycle rules; do not let search/view/favorite mutation create a time record.
needs.status: precise reversible contract proposed; terminology and eight-item preview require product/user validation

needs.need: Move the user’s catalog labels, aliases, parent/order choices and quick-access shortcuts to another device without losing the destination’s independent history or silently replacing local customizations.
needs.design_response: Add separately versioned catalog-only package and previewed stable-ID merge; keep source definitions and personal overlay distinguishable.
needs.status: schema and deterministic conflict policy proposed; implementation and round-trip unverified

needs.need: Let seed translations and hierarchy revisions improve search while preserving a person’s own labels/aliases and historical classifications.
needs.design_response: Use stable IDs and explicit local override/provenance; new semantic identity gets new ID; do not match by label or reclassify history on catalog update.
needs.status: existing history rule documented; override provenance and seed-update migration remain unimplemented/unverified

alternatives.name: Flat compact grid/list only
benefits: Fast direct taps for small catalogues
costs: Scroll burden as the list grows
Same names need an additional disambiguator
alternatives.assessment: Suitable as quick-start surface, insufficient as the only navigation for an eventual large catalogue.

alternatives.name: Nested tree/folder-only picker
costs: Can hide a valid item under an unexpected parent
A full tree may be premature during onboarding
alternatives.assessment: Good optional Browse mode; do not require folder construction at first start.

alternatives.name: Independent tags only
benefits: Can filter across parents and shared activities
costs: Does not supply a parent path or natural tree roll-up
Too many choice chips may create tag chores
alternatives.assessment: Use as optional facets, not a substitute for grouping semantics.

alternatives.name: Global all-catalog search with optional current-folder/tag filter
benefits: Can expose personal aliases and paths
costs: More results require ranking and duplicate-name paths
alternatives.assessment: Best search default to prototype; folder/tag filtering should be explicit, never silently scoped.

alternatives.name: One-touch recents and manual favorites
benefits: Recency updates itself; favorite order stays under user control
Does not hide the rest of the catalogue
alternatives.assessment: Preferred lightweight quick-access pattern; recent and favorite definitions must remain separate.

alternatives.name: Automatically sort full list by frequency/recent activity
benefits: Could place reusable actions closer without manual curation
costs: Frequency time window and definition of activity are ambiguous
Could repeatedly surface old one-off actions
alternatives.assessment: Do not default to it; offer only after a user choice and with clear sort label/window.

alternatives.name: Fuzzy/phonetic matching as primary retrieval
benefits: Can recover misspelled or partially remembered names
costs: False positives, English-language bias, uncertain locale behavior, possibly expensive candidate generation
alternatives.assessment: Secondary, marked candidate retrieval only; exact name/alias stays ahead, no automatic label mapping.

alternatives.name: Combined global search, optional Browse tree, independent facets, personal aliases, stable favorites, timestamped recents
benefits: Supports novices immediately and power users later
Separates hierarchy, cross-cutting tags and quick access
costs: Requires careful filter/path/ranking design and local tests
alternatives.assessment: Recommended prototype direction; not approved implementation scope.

alternatives.name: Full backup restore versus catalog-only merge
benefits: Full backup preserves whole dataset for device recovery.
Catalog-only mode can bring search structure and personal quick access without changing target history.
costs: Full restore is a complete replacement and may remove newer local records.
Catalog-only merge needs per-ID preview, overlay provenance, conflict/dependency reporting and explicit shortcut merge rules.
alternatives.assessment: Keep both as named, separate actions. Never implement “catalog only” by invoking full replacement restore; do not imply addCatalog alone is a user-facing portable package.

risks.risk: Search field scope is unclear or silently confined to one group/type.
risks.mechanism: User enters task label in a project-only field and sees no result; repeated navigation and scrolling.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Global all-items scope by default; label any current-folder or facet limit; show full path.

risks.risk: Overly aggressive typo/accent/transliteration matching selects or suggests a semantically different activity.
risks.mechanism: String similarity is not intent and language-specific letter equivalence differs.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Original label preserved; ranking tiers; approximate label; no auto-start or auto-category mapping from query alone.

risks.risk: High-cardinality suggestions delay input or drop keystrokes.
risks.mechanism: Heavy query/render on each character; excessive rows focusable at once.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Indexed/local data, throttle/debounce when needed, incremental render, bounded visible suggestions and full scrollable results; test 10k synthetic input.

risks.risk: Manual drag reorder becomes the only route to keep a frequent activity at the top.
risks.mechanism: Long-range drag and scrolling are tedious and may be inaccessible.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Favorites and recent row; Move to top / reorder accessibility action; manual, alphabetical and explicit recent order choices.

risks.risk: Frequency sorting makes stable catalogue items jump unexpectedly.
risks.mechanism: Recency window and count definition are unclear; user activity changes each day.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Use explicit Favorite and timestamped Recent separately; frequency sorting only opt-in with period label.

risks.risk: A copied full database conflates portable setup with personal time history.
risks.mechanism: A user seeking only reusable activity definitions has no narrow payload.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Separate export choices and preview imported IDs/duplicates before applying; let the user choose history payload.

risks.risk: Favorites, recents, history entries and full entry templates are collapsed into one feature.
risks.mechanism: A named activity favorite is not the same as a complete start with tags/description/default values.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Separate labels and interactions; preview all fields of a saved full-entry shortcut.

risks.risk: Accessibility path disappears in a dense grid or gestures-only list.
risks.mechanism: Screen-reader users need sequential navigation and long container exit; motor-access users may not drag.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Semantics/state/path, 48dp targets, TalkBack, Switch Access/Voice Access alternate custom actions, large-font review.

risks.risk: UI localization silently changes user-created names or seed aliases.
risks.mechanism: Translated resources and persistent user data are stored/handled as if they were the same field.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Keep original labels and aliases separate from UI locale; test language changes and restore without relabeling.

risks.risk: Tags are mistaken for categories or counted as additional time totals.
risks.mechanism: Cross-cutting filters are treated as parents or additive buckets.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Visualize path only for actual hierarchy; tag is a filter/facet badge; reconcile primary totals according to existing product data model.

risks.risk: Seed translations leave default onboarding labels unreadable or inconsistent.
risks.mechanism: UI supports a language while sample activity labels remain English.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Translate seed display resources; preserve the user's chosen label; allow no translation/locale to block start.

risks.risk: The UI uses “favorite” for an item, selection snapshot and completed time entry interchangeably.
risks.mechanism: The user may expect rename-safe live reference but instead get frozen parameters, or remove a convenience and assume history was deleted.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Use separate labels and controls for favorite item, saved start preset and historical entry; test each removal independently.

risks.risk: Catalog import guesses identity from equal names or silently overwrites a user rename/parent/alias with a translation refresh.
risks.mechanism: Different tasks are merged; historical IDs/rollups appear to change meaning; personal search words disappear.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Use stable entity IDs plus explicit override/provenance; report conflict by field; default to preserve destination values; no silent history remap.

risks.risk: A whole-backup restore is used as a shortcut to transfer catalog, erasing newer local history.
risks.mechanism: Restore replaces existing dataset instead of merging definitions.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Distinct export labels/discriminators and a preview stating history counts and replacement versus merge; keep history untouched in catalog-only mode.

risks.risk: Imported shortcut/pin references a conflicting axis, value, parent, or archived type and is attached to the wrong local definition.
risks.mechanism: An entry appears valid by text but changes the selected classification/detail.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Validate graph before commit; block dependent imports on unresolved identity conflict; show full path and meaning version.

risks.risk: Recent ordering is imported as though it were complete time history or merged by incomparable rank/timestamps.
risks.mechanism: New device shows a fabricated last-used time or unpredictable order.
risks.mitigation_to_test: Catalog-only bundle may carry only an explicit ID order; do not fabricate timestamp/history; default to destination Recent on merge.

acceptance_scenarios.expected: Start a visible seeded action and save its timestamp with no group, tag or alias required; Search/All/Add stay visible.
Empty results do not block current timer stop or future start; user can add a name or keep it unclassified and relabel later.
A named task can be found without first choosing its assumed type/folder; any scope filter is explicit.
Each result has visible and spoken full path and stable user label.
Search results show whether match was label, alias, path or tag; facets do not modify labels.
Favorite order remains stable while the full list does not silently reorder with each timer use.
Most recently started action appears first; actions falling off the compact recent view remain in All/history.
If available, the user chooses sort mode and sees its time window; returning to Manual/A-Z is straightforward.
The UI makes it clear if a favorite starts only an activity or restores multiple entry fields; preview fields before start.
Approximate match appears only as a labeled candidate; exact label/alias ranks higher; no auto-start or relabel occurs.
Switching UI locale does not mutate a stored custom label; a user alias in either script finds the same item and shows the original label.
Canonical/case matching behaves consistently for chosen locale fixtures; distinctions meaningful in the tested language are not silently collapsed.
Folder path and cross-cutting tag are visibly distinct; a tag filter does not become a parent roll-up.
Breadcrumb/back works; global search from within a folder can still find an item outside it or clearly displays a current-folder filter.
At synthetic sizes 100, 1,000 and 10,000, keyboard input does not block or lose characters; long result list renders incrementally. Define latency thresholds by prototype test.
High-cardinality comment or alias suggestions do not overlay the keyboard, freeze input, or steal typed characters; user can narrow scope by current activity.
For the Android app, TalkBack is the primary screen-reader test with Switch Access/Voice Access as needed. VoiceOver is tested only if an Apple client is in scope, not counted as Android acceptance.
Every action is sequentially reachable; label, path and favorite state are spoken; user can exit long container, focus/clear search and start a result.
